status_rationale: Gate C approved and Lean mapping v7 exists in namespace Spec2Lean.PTX.OrB32. This artifact only proposes theorem obligations (no proofs) for the next THEOREM_STRENGTH review; no code beyond candidate JSON is changed.

unit.bounded_unit: PTX ISA 9.3 bounded unit `or.b32 d, a, b;`
unit.scope_boundary: Only .b32 bounded semantics with optional predicate guard and a register-file + predicate-file state model are in scope.

compliance_notes: No proofs are included at this stage.
No vacuous function-totality claims: determinism is stated over the relation OrB32Step.
No semantics are imported from unrelated units.

validation_obligations.title: Bounded instruction structure and operand order
validation_obligations.description: or.b32 instruction includes optional guard and exactly destination then source1 then source2 fields (d, a, b), with source1 register-only and source2 register-or-immediate in this bounded mapping.

validation_obligations.title: 32-bit bounded value representation
validation_obligations.description: B32 is represented as Fin (2^32), enforcing the bounded scalar width in type.

validation_obligations.title: Minimal machine state and partial outcome
validation_obligations.description: MachineState contains only valueRegs and predRegs maps; execOrB32 returns Option outcomes and none for malformed or missing inputs.

theorem_obligations.intent: One-step relation is deterministic for fixed (s, i).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For all s, i, s1, s2, if OrB32Step s i s1 and OrB32Step s i s2 then s1 = s2.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : OrB32Step s i s1) (h2 : OrB32Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation has meaningful constructors for guard-false and executed cases, so equality of post-state is a substantive property, not function extensionality.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case split on h1 and h2; constructor mismatch gives contradiction on evalGuard results, constructor match reduces to definitional equality of updateDestination and read values.

theorem_obligations.intent: Relate execOrB32 Option outcomes to OrB32Step.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: Executed/guard-false outcomes from execOrB32 correspond to OrB32Step; every step is produced by some execOrB32 outcome; none occurs iff no step exists.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execOrB32_executed_sound (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) : OrB32Step s i s'
/-- similar lemmas for guard-false and completeness /--
hypotheses: h : execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')
h2 : execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.notExecuted s')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Function/relation consistency for success and no-op outcomes, and partial completeness with none.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: execOrB32 is partial and includes an explicit none branch; this gives both non-empty and empty relation cases for meaningful correspondence.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execOrB32 and OrB32Step, then by cases on evalGuard and source reads.

theorem_obligations.intent: Under true guard and resolvable sources, executed state contains destination written with OR of resolved source values.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If evalGuard is true, destination is register r, and both sources read to va/vb, then execOrB32 returns executed state whose register r equals orValue va vb.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem execOrB32_or_result_correct (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B32) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) (ha : readSource1 s i.a = some va) (hb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb) : ∃ s', execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (orValue va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : readSource1 s i.a = some va
hb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Destination register receives bitwise OR result exactly at the post-state.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The claim pins the concrete arithmetic result to the semantics phrase d = a | b and therefore is stronger than mere state-change existence.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: From hguard, ha, hb unfold execOrB32 and `hd` to identify executed branch and evaluate updateDestination.

theorem_obligations.intent: When destination is bitBucket, a successful executed step preserves the whole state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any step OrB32Step s i s' with i.d = Destination.bitBucket, we have s' = s.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32Step_bitBucket_preserves_state (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket) : s' = s
theorem_obligations.conclusion: The state is unchanged when destination is `_`.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: updateDestination has an explicit bitBucket no-op branch; this theorem checks that behavior at relation level.
strength_risks: This relies on the bounded-design inference AMB-1/AMB-2: `_` support is accepted by instruction-family syntax, not an explicit per-unit statement for or.b32.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Rewrite hd and simplify updateDestination in executed constructor; guard-false case is immediate from the constructor definition.

theorem_obligations.intent: A true-guard executed step updates only value registers (destination) and leaves predicate state unchanged.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If OrB32Step s i s' is the executed case and both sources are available, then for all p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32Step_executed_preserves_predicates (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (va vb : B32) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hasa : readSource1 s i.a = some va) (hasb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb) : ∀ p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
hasa : readSource1 s i.a = some va
hasb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Predicate register map is identical in the post-state.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The architecture excludes predicate writes in this bounded unit, so predicate invariance is a useful frame property and not a tautology of the instruction definition alone.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Only executed-constructor branch updates via updateDestination which changes only valueRegs.
